title: Activating Nonstandard Axion Electrodynamics in Topological Insulator Materials
authors: Miklós Horváth, Long Liang, Panagiotis Kotetes
abstract: The conventional axion response of topological insulators (TIs) is characterized by an isotropic pseudoscalar magnetoelectric (ME) coupling rooted in band topology: the condensed matter analog of the axion field. However, as we reveal here, this and other more general ME responses can arise in existing TI materials from symmetry breaking without requiring nontrivial topology. Indeed, we show that breaking parity and time-reversal symmetries using combined electric and magnetic fields unlocks nonstandard axion electrodynamics via the controllable activation of various tensorial ME couplings, thus, going beyond the standard axion picture. Using a well-established first-principles-informed effective model for Bi-and Sb-based TI materials, we estimate the resulting ME coefficients and make concrete predictions for experiments. In particular, we identify nonreciprocal directional dichroism as a distinctive magneto-optical signature of these ME effects, therefore opening a route to engineer and probe symmetry-induced ME phenomena beyond the conventional topological response.
summary: This work shows that nonstandard axion electrodynamics can be activated in topological insulators by applying combined electric and magnetic fields, even if the material lacks intrinsic magnetic order. The key prediction is the observation of nonreciprocal directional dichroism (NDD) in light propagation, offering a tunable, symmetry-controlled signature beyond the standard topological response.
main_problem: To reveal an original and experimentally straightforward strategy to activate nonstandard axion electrodynamics (AED) effects in topological insulator (TI) materials, going beyond the standard axion picture.
main_result: Applying combined static electric ($\mathbf{E}$) and magnetic ($\mathbf{B}$) fields activates a nonstandard, tensorial magnetoelectric (ME) coupling ($\Theta_{ij}$), leading to nonreciprocal directional dichroism (NDD) as a measurable magneto-optical signature.
method: The authors use a low-energy $\mathbf{k} \cdot \mathbf{p}$ model and Green's function formalism to derive the effective Hamiltonian and analyze the resulting electromagnetic wave propagation equations.
model_or_system: The system is 3D TI materials, specifically Bi- and Sb-based families, modeled using a continuum Hamiltonian extended to include linear couplings to external $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ fields ($\propto E_i, B_i, E_i B_j$).
key_observables: Nonreciprocal directional dichroism (NDD) in the dispersion relation ($\omega \propto 1 \pm 	ext{sgn}(\mathbf{q})\eta_{\Theta}$), and the tensorial ME coefficients ($\Theta_{ij}$).
important_parameters: The effect is tunable by the applied $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ fields, and the predicted relative speed difference for NDD is in the $10^{-7} - 10^{-4}$ range.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on treating external fields perturbatively and retaining only terms linear in $\mathbf{E}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ (dropping $E^2$ and $B^2$ terms).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical setup for measuring NDD ($\mathbf{q} \perp \mathbf{E} \perp \mathbf{B}$) and sketch the required field configurations to observe the non-standard ME effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the need to go beyond standard axion coupling, deriving the field-modified Hamiltonian, calculating the resulting ME tensor ($\Theta_{ij}$), and finally analyzing the consequences for EM wave propagation, predicting NDD as the key experimental signature.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer and probe symmetry-induced ME phenomena using external fields in TIs provides a clean platform for studying topological responses, which is relevant to controlling quantum states via external fields.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Nonstandard AED in P- and T -symmetric 3D TI materials activated by combined static electric E and magnetic B fields. The engineered axion behavior manifests itself as a controllable nonre- ciprocal directional dichroism (NDD). (a) When E||B, diagonal ele- ments of the ME tensor are obtained, and the EM wave propagation is affected by the ME coupling only for fields applied perpendicu- lar to the wave vector q. In this case, the light velocities for linear polarizations parallel to the yz-plane diagonals are distinct and non- reciprocal. (b) For B ⊥E ⊥q, it is off-diagonal elements of the ME tensor that become generated, and lead to analogous NDD effects.
